figures.alt: Nested boundary from model capability through model component and product behavior to an outcome authorized by named decision owners.
figures.caption: F01.1 - Product accountability begins at observable combined behavior, while outcome authorization remains explicitly assigned.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Recursive evidence loop from task and behavior contract through mechanism, evaluation, release, operation, feedback, and controlled change.
figures.caption: F01.2 - Every later observation can return the team to an earlier decision without erasing the evidence trail.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Task anatomy connecting actor, trigger, context, decision, baseline, friction, consequence, affected groups, and evidence.
figures.caption: F02.1 - A task brief makes the current path and consequence visible before any AI mechanism is chosen.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Hypothesis tree separating user value, product behavior, adoption, operations, and business assumptions with disconfirmation paths.
figures.caption: F02.2 - The next experiment targets the uncertainty most likely to change the build, narrow, or stop decision.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Behavior state model showing required response, clarification, abstention, escalation, degraded mode, and prohibited action states.
figures.caption: F03.1 - Uncertainty becomes explicit system behavior instead of being hidden behind a fluent answer.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Authority map separating system suggestion, user correction, specialist review, domain decision, formal authorization, and execution.
figures.caption: F03.2 - Review supplies evidence; only a named role with the relevant decision right can authorize consequence.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Decision ladder comparing rules, lexical and structured retrieval, predictive scoring, multimodal retrieval, ranking, generation, and tools without treating them as maturity stages.
figures.caption: F04.1 - Move only when the current option cannot satisfy a contract clause and the next option can earn its added burden.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Tradeoff frontier showing task quality, consequential error, latency tail, cost, privacy, attack surface, operability, change risk, and fallback for several mechanism portfolios.
figures.caption: F04.2 - There is no universal best model; acceptable portfolios occupy different positions under a specific task and operating context.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Nested view of intended task population, observed sample, label process, and intersecting analysis segments, with unknown and excluded groups kept visible.
figures.caption: F05.1 - A valid sample can still leave unsupported groups, unknown populations, and consequential intersections outside its evidence.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Leakage path map separating source population, development, tuning, evaluator development, challenge, and frozen release evaluation, with prohibited duplicate, time, label, feature, and reviewer paths.
figures.caption: F05.2 - Release evidence remains credible only when content, labels, features, time, reviewers, and evaluator development cannot carry answers across the freeze.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Retrieval pipeline separating query transformation, source selection, candidate generation, permission and freshness filters, ranking, context assembly, downstream use, user evidence, and trace.
figures.caption: F06.1 - Each stage creates a distinct failure and evidence surface, so a product regression can be localized instead of blamed on the model.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Decision tree routing authorized fresh evidence to ranking, stale evidence to degraded behavior, conflicting evidence to abstention or domain escalation, unauthorized evidence to exclusion, and absent evidence to safe fallback.
figures.caption: F06.2 - Stale, conflicting, unauthorized, and absent evidence are distinct product states and none permits a generated substitute.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Colorful layered three-dimensional architecture showing the user interface, application, authorized data and retrieval, learned adapter, deterministic policy, presentation, tool gateway, trace, and named human authorities as distinct connected zones.
figures.caption: F07.1 - Learned components propose evidence and wording; deterministic boundaries validate scope, policy, state, and effects before consequence.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Vivid three-dimensional boundary map with untrusted inputs outside, validated data and deterministic control in the center, product state and draft-only tools beyond gated checkpoints, and named owners and authorities connected to each gate.
figures.caption: F07.2 - Trust, state, and authority are separate dimensions and each transition needs a validator, state owner, failure disposition, and authority.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Crisp colorful three-dimensional path following one request through identity, validation, retrieval, deterministic policy, provider envelope, result validation, presentation, and trace, with bright side branches for abstention, timeout, invalid output, and authorization failure.
figures.caption: F08.1 - Every hop emits a state and reason; failure branches terminate before a result or effect.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Playful realistic three-dimensional exploded view of a structured result, with separate layers for schema, candidate evidence, policy state, explanation, permissions, versions, trace, and a locked zero-effect chamber.
figures.caption: F08.2 - Shape, semantic policy, permission, current state, and effect gating remain separately validated layers.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Colorful tactile three-dimensional coverage board connecting behavior clauses, user segments, data states, mechanisms, and consequences to evaluation-case tiles, with bright empty cells deliberately visible.
figures.caption: F09.1 - A case count cannot show which clauses, segments, states, mechanisms, and consequences remain unsupported.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Bright realistic three-dimensional circular workshop showing case discovery, permission review, construction, grouping, split freeze, evaluation, decision, production learning, refresh, and retirement, with a sealed release set and visible contamination alarm.
figures.caption: F09.2 - Provenance, grouping, freeze, decision use, refresh, and retirement remain visible throughout the evaluation-set lifecycle.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Colorful three-dimensional error topology connecting irrelevant, incompatible, unsupported, stale, overconfident, and correct-abstention states to consequence, segment, detectability, reversibility, control, and disposition.
figures.caption: F10.1 - Error categories become useful when they connect to consequence, segment, control, and disposition.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Bright three-dimensional threshold surface with essential labels for false match, abstention, coverage, critical segment recall, and permission/incompatibility violations across operating points.
figures.caption: F10.2 - A threshold is an operating policy, not a hidden tuning constant.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Colorful three-dimensional judgment stack routing claim evidence through deterministic check, reference comparison, model grader, trained rater, specialist, and a separate authority gate, with disagreement and limitation stops.
figures.caption: F11.1 - Use the cheapest credible evidence for each claim while keeping authority separate.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Bright three-dimensional calibration flow from a calibration set through blind sample, human judgment, model judgment, disagreement, adjudication, and limitation, with position bias, verbosity bias, and unresolved states visible.
figures.caption: F11.2 - A scalable evaluator earns only limited, local trust.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Colorful three-dimensional experiment graph connecting preregistration and a versioned baseline to paired-change and ablation paths, routing a confounded path to quarantine before segment results and decision.
figures.caption: F12.1 - An experiment graph exposes what changed and what must remain comparable.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani

figures.alt: Bright three-dimensional decision flow carrying versioned result packets through result, uncertainty, segments, guardrails, confounds, and negative evidence to an authority gate and five explicit dispositions.
figures.caption: F12.2 - Results are unfinished until they change an explicit decision.
figures.creator: Komal Nakrani
